source: Lin, Snell, Stoica, Gonzalez et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
finding: Closest working analogue of incubation in an LLM loop. The model thinks offline about a context before the question arrives, and the rewritten context is reused at test time.
numbers: Same accuracy with about 5x less test-time compute on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME. Scaling sleep-time compute adds up to +13% (GSM-Symbolic) and +18% (AIME).
limits: Math tasks built by splitting a problem into context plus question. Not a creative or insight task. It is pre-computation, not forgetting.
agent_relevance: A cheap scheduled idle pass can be code-triggered between turns. It must be tied to a likely future query, not run blindly.

source: Lin, Snell, Stoica, Gonzalez et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
finding: Gain depends on whether the future query is predictable from the context. Unpredictable queries gain little.
numbers: Accuracy gap between sleep-time and test-time-only widens as question predictability (Llama2-70B log-prob) rises, shown across five quantile bins on P1 and P2. For parallel sleep generations, 5 generally beat 10.
limits: Predictability proxy is a base-model log-probability. Authors say unrelated queries should use plain test-time scaling.
agent_relevance: Mirrors the human view that incubation helps only when the problem is already loaded and the person is stuck. Run a sleep pass only after a real impasse on a known question (fits G1).

source: Lin, Snell, Stoica, Gonzalez et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
finding: Amortising one sleep pass over several questions on the same context lowers cost per question.
numbers: Average cost per query down 2.5x on Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic (2, 5 and 10 questions per context tested).
limits: Extra questions were generated by o3-mini, so they may be more tied to the context than real user questions.
agent_relevance: Reuse of a re-represented context across later sub-questions is a cheap operator for the schema.

source: Lin, Snell, Stoica, Gonzalez et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
finding: On a realistic agent task the benefit reverses at high budget.
numbers: SWE-Features: up to about 1.5x fewer test-time tokens at low budget. At high test-time budget, test-time-only had higher precision and comparable recall. Sleep-time agents edited more files.
limits: Scored by F1 of the predicted file set, not by tests. Authors give a hypothesis, not a test, for the cause.
agent_relevance: Offline exploration can anchor the agent on a wide or wrong frame. That is a machine version of fixation, so keep a reset option.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
finding: Reported aha moment: during RL the model suddenly starts to rethink with words like wait. Presented as an insight-like event.
numbers: R1-Zero AIME 2024 pass@1 rose from 15.6% to 77.9% during training. Reflective words rose 5 to 7 fold. The word wait was near absent early, occasional at steps 4000-7000, with spikes after step 8000.
quote: Wait, wait. Wait. That's an aha moment I can flag here.
limits: Counts a word, not a measured change of representation. Insight in the human sense (restructuring) is not tested. The label is the authors' own.
agent_relevance: A rethink token is a cheap re-entry point. But we should trigger it by code on a signal, not on a schedule.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Understanding Aha Moments: from External Observations to Internal Mechanisms
finding: Compares aha models with no-aha models. Aha models use more human-like self-reflection and adjust stated uncertainty to difficulty.
numbers: Reasoning-collapse rates (language mixing, repeated language, repeated reasoning path) measured over 200 test samples per difficulty level. Aha models near zero for language mixing and path repetition at difficulty 3-6. At low difficulty aha models repeat more (overthinking easy problems).
limits: Preprint. Collapse detection uses heuristics (non-English characters, repeats, phrase similarity). Causal role of the aha tone is argued from latent analysis, not from an intervention.
agent_relevance: Reflection style helps most when the problem is hard and hurts on easy ones. Supports gating rethink on difficulty (G1).

source: Yang et al. (2025) Understanding Aha Moments: from External Observations to Internal Mechanisms
finding: Internal view: the perceived difficulty of a problem shifts across layers.
numbers: As layer depth rises, easy problems look more complex and hard problems look simpler to the probe. Anthropomorphic and pure-reasoning features separate.
limits: Probe-based, one model family. Not a replication of human insight measures.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence that a reframe changes how the model represents difficulty. Do not build on it yet.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling
finding: Budget forcing: when the model tries to stop, append Wait so it keeps thinking. This is a forced rethink, a crude incubation-like reset.
numbers: s1-32B AIME24 50.0% to 56.7% with budget forcing (57% in the abstract). Ablation of the appended string: no extrapolation 50.0 AIME / 93.0 MATH500 / 57.6 GPQA; ignoring the stop twice with no string 50.0 / 90.2 / 55.1; Wait gave the best result.
limits: One model, 1,000 SFT examples. Gains stop and later reverse beyond a few forced continuations. Authors note longer samples are often wrong ones.
agent_relevance: Forced continuation helps a little then plateaus. Cap it in code.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling
finding: Authors suspect short correct generations are on the right track from the start, while long ones backtrack and are wrong.
numbers: Under rejection sampling at the smaller token budget the model jumps to the correct approach; at the larger budget it backtracks a lot and is wrong more often (inverse scaling in that setting).
limits: Hypothesis from one worked example, not a controlled test.
agent_relevance: Long persistence is a warning sign for fixation on a wrong frame, not a sign of progress.

source: Ghosal et al. (2025) Does Thinking More Always Help? Mirage of Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning Models
finding: Extending thinking with Wait or Think more first helps, then hurts. Gains come from higher output variance, not better reasoning.
numbers: Accuracy 82.2% to 87.3% as thinking tokens go 385 to 1100, then falls to 70.3% at 15,980 tokens. R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on GSM-8K: Wait-and-Think-More to 16,000 tokens gives -11.8%; parallel thinking at the same budget gives +10.1%.
limits: Mostly small distilled reasoning models and math sets. The probabilistic model is simple.
agent_relevance: Direct machine analogue of unreliable incubation: more time is not better, and benefit is inconsistent. Prefer independent restarts to long sequential continuation.

source: Ghosal et al. (2025) Does Thinking More Always Help? Mirage of Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning Models
finding: Parallel independent attempts with majority vote beat sequential extension at equal token budget.
numbers: Up to 20% higher accuracy than extended thinking (abstract); the text also quotes 22% and 47% for some models at a 16K budget.
limits: Same-model samples are not independent (our G4). Vote is code-side and works only for single-answer tasks.
agent_relevance: Supports fresh restart as the machine form of incubation, with code selecting. Watch G4.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Thoughts Are All Over the Place: On the Underthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Opposite failure to fixation: o1-like models switch strategy too often and abandon promising paths. Wrong answers contain far more switches.
numbers: On AIME2024, wrong responses use 225% more tokens and 418% more thought switches than right ones. Underthinking scores: QwQ-32B-Preview 65.0 on AIME24; DeepSeek-R1-671B 65.4 on MATH500-Hard.
limits: Metric defined by the authors (share of tokens after the first correct thought). Open models only.
agent_relevance: Switching frames is not incubation. Without a signal it is noise. Fits G1: reframe only on a real signal.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Thoughts Are All Over the Place: On the Underthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: A decoding penalty on thought-switch tokens (TIP) raises accuracy without training.
numbers: AIME2024 pass@1: QwQ-32B-Preview 38.3 to 44.1; R1-Distill-Qwen-32B 61.4 to 64.1; DeepSeek-R1 73.8 to 74.8. Switch tokens fell (R1-Distill 13.8 to 5.7 per the table). A prompt-only version for DeepSeek-R1 gave 72.4, below baseline.
limits: 32 samples, temperature 0.7. Gains shrink at high pass@k. Table was garbled in text extraction; row alignment checked by eye.
agent_relevance: Staying with a frame longer on purpose has measurable value. Counterweight to always reframe.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
finding: Constructed tasks where longer reasoning lowers accuracy. Five failure modes. Several match fixation or misleading-clue effects.
numbers: Task families: counting with distractors, regression with spurious features, deduction with constraint tracking, AI-risk. Claude models get more distracted by irrelevant information with longer reasoning; o-series resist distractors but overfit to problem framing; models drift from sensible priors to spurious features.
limits: Tasks were built to show the effect. Not a measure of how common it is on ordinary tasks.
agent_relevance: The classic incubation story says rest removes misleading clues. Here extra thinking adds them. The remedy is a clean restart without the earlier trace, not more tokens.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: A planted misleading clue (GSM-IC) cuts accuracy. This is the machine version of the misleading clue that Ward says incubation lets people forget.
numbers: No more than 18% of baseline-solved problems stay solved under all irrelevant-context types; macro accuracy under 30% for both models tested. Best macro accuracy with self-consistency: 45% (20 samples).
limits: 2022-era models (code-davinci-002, text-davinci-003). Newer reasoning models not tested here.
agent_relevance: Cleaning context (dropping the earlier trace) is the machine analogue of forgetting. Test it.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Fixes that work: self-consistency, exemplars with distractors, and an explicit instruction to ignore irrelevant information.
numbers: Correct answer present in 99.7% of 20 samples for CoT and LTM; 96.5% for 0-CoT. Exemplars with distractors gave +35.5 points micro accuracy on 0-CoT. Instructed prompting improved CoT, LTM and program prompts.
limits: Sample recall is not accuracy; a verifier is still needed.
agent_relevance: Generate many, pick in code. The right answer is usually already in the pool.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Verification stage without an external signal fails. Re-looking at an answer does not reliably fix it.
numbers: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 standard, 75.1 after self-correct round 1, 74.7 after round 2 (3 and 5 calls). CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 to 41.8. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0. With an oracle label, GPT-3.5 reached 84.3 on GSM8K (this row is the oracle-stopped condition).
limits: Older GPT models. Oracle gains come from stopping when right, which is not available in practice.
agent_relevance: Supports G2: revise only from real output. Verification in Wallas terms needs a code check.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Among changed answers, the model is more likely to turn a right answer into a wrong one.
numbers: GSM8K: GPT-3.5 keeps its first answer 74.7% of the time across two rounds.
limits: Prompt-dependent. Later work shows gains when feedback is external.
agent_relevance: A second look stage with no check is a net loss.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
finding: Reflection step: agents periodically synthesise raw memories into higher-level statements. A built-in consolidation stage, close to the preparation-to-illumination idea.
numbers: Trigger: when the sum of importance scores passes a threshold. Believability TrueSkill: full 29.89, no reflection 26.88, no reflection or planning 25.64, crowdworker 22.95, no memory/planning/reflection 21.21. Full vs prior-work baseline d = 8.16.
limits: Rated by 100 Prolific judges on believability, not task success. Reflection effect is one ablation step (about 3 points).
agent_relevance: Reflection fired by a counted threshold (not by the model) matches our rule that code decides transitions.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Verbal reflection after a failed trial, stored and re-read on the next try. Needs an external pass or fail signal.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80%. AlfWorld +22% in 12 steps, HotPotQA +20%. Self-reflection ablation: +8% absolute over episodic memory alone.
limits: Gains depend on environment feedback or unit tests; Huang et al. show they vanish without it.
agent_relevance: A real-output-triggered reflect-and-retry loop. The signal is the point, not the rest period.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
finding: Explicit search with backtracking lets the model abandon a wrong frame. A machine form of impasse and restructuring.
numbers: Game of 24: chain-of-thought solved 4%, Tree of Thoughts 74% (breadth 5); breadth 1 gives 45%. GPT-4 generation plus GPT-3.5 evaluation: 64%.
limits: Needs a state evaluator. Costly in calls. The task has a clean verifier.
agent_relevance: Where a verifier exists, search beats rest.

source: Bellemare-Pepin et al. (2024) Divergent Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models
finding: Divergent word task (DAT): GPT-4 beats the average of about 100,000 humans, still short of highly creative people. Temperature raises scores.
numbers: GPT-4 above the human mean with significance; GeminiPro indistinguishable from humans; GPT-4-turbo worse than GPT-4. GPT-4 at temperature 1.5: mean 85.6, higher than 72% of human scores (n = 500 generations per temperature: 0.5, 1.0, 1.5). 70% of GPT-4 responses contain the word microscope.
limits: Measures divergent generation, not incubation or insight. Word-list task only.
agent_relevance: Diversity is a sampling knob. Rest is not needed to get it. Repeated words show samples from one model overlap (G4).

source: Jiang et al. (2023) BRAINTEASER: Lateral Thinking Puzzles for Large Language Models
finding: Insight-like riddles that need breaking a default commonsense frame. Models are far below humans.
numbers: 1,100 puzzles. Sentence puzzles: human about 91% instance accuracy and 88.9% group-based; ChatGPT 60.8% original, 59.3% semantic reconstruction, 67.9% context reconstruction. ChatGPT overall 53% and 63% on the two subtasks, between random 25% and human 92%.
limits: Multiple choice. 2023 models. Human number from 102 sampled items. Column alignment of the extracted table is uncertain.
agent_relevance: The frame-breaking step is weak in single-pass models. Consistency under rewording is the harder test.

source: Ellis et al. (2020) DreamCoder: Growing generalizable, interpretable knowledge with wake-sleep Bayesian program learning
finding: Older AI system built on a sleep idea: wake solves tasks, sleep replays and imagines problems to grow a library and retrain the guide network.
numbers: Applied across eight domains including list processing, text editing, and physics equations. Sleep adds abstractions that shorten later search.
limits: Sleep here is learning between tasks, not forgetting of misleading clues. No test of incubation effects as such.
agent_relevance: Offline consolidation between episodes is an old, working design. Matches idle-time library building for the agent.

source: Helie and Sun (2010) Incubation, insight, and creative problem solving: a unified theory and a connectionist model
finding: Psychological Review paper giving a CLARION-based computational model of incubation and insight. Citation confirmed through a secondary page only; contents not read.
numbers: Not read. Vol 117 issue 3, pages 994-1024.
limits: Not opened; do not cite numbers.
agent_relevance: Possible template for a two-track agent (implicit track, explicit track). Read before relying on it.

source: Gap note for this angle
finding: I found no study that tests a Wallas-style incubation break in an LLM on human incubation paradigms (RAT or insight problems with and without a delay). Search APIs were rate limited and web search was out of budget, so the gap is not proven. Nearest items are sleep-time compute, reflection, forced Wait, and restart-style parallel sampling.
numbers: None.
limits: Absence of results after blocked search is weak evidence. Rerun with working search before stating there is no such work.
agent_relevance: Treat incubation for the agent as an untested design choice [D], to be measured on our own tasks.
